question: m14
q: How has the Aussie dollar moved against the US dollar and the euro since the start of 2026?

transcript.answer:
The Aussie dollar is up against both currencies since the start of 2026, more so against the euro.

| | Dec 2025 (start) | Latest (Oct 2026) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| A$1 in US dollars | 0.6693 | 0.6947 | up about 3.8% |
| A$1 in euros | 0.5704 | 0.6187 | up about 8.5% |

The start point is the December 2025 month-end rate. The latest figure is the last October 2026 observation in the RBA data, which may not be a full month.

The gap between the two moves means the euro has weakened against the US dollar. Using the two rates, one euro bought about US$1.173 at the end of 2025 and about US$1.123 in October 2026, a fall of roughly 4%.

Within the year, the AUD/USD rate has ranged from a low of 0.6845 in March to a high of 0.7166 in August. It has eased since August, to 0.6977 in September and 0.6947 in October. The AUD/EUR rate has risen fairly steadily, with its low at the start of the year and its high at the latest observation.
